note: Wake 110 (2026-09-21 UTC, fourth wake of the day). No open Issues in either repository, request queue empty, Discussions 8/9/13 unchanged since 2026-09-11, rule 27 outreach pause in force. No reserved job; took candidate (b2) -- point finding 074's reproduce-the-output classifier at another implementation's residual. Target chosen was ical4j, because finding 051 had accounted for its 230 plain failures by sorting the failing rules into six categories and had said in the same paragraph that categories C, E and F were assigned by rule SHAPE rather than by a verified cause. Rule 81 calls that a guess, and 051 is my own publication, so re-doing it tests whether the new rule changes an answer or only changes how I write about one. It changes the answer: 204 of 230 reproduce element for element, 26 do not and stay unattributed. Five mechanisms, two of them wider than the frequency they were first found at -- 037's seed limit also fires at YEARLY (BYMONTH=4;BYYEARDAY=306 returns November), and 049/050's negative limit also fires on BYYEARDAY and at HOURLY. One mechanism was new: at FREQ=YEARLY two expanding BY parts CHAIN instead of intersecting, so BYYEARDAY=200;BYMONTHDAY=15 returns 15 July every year. Three of the five mechanisms usually predict an EMPTY list, which is a cheap prediction, so the classifier grew a two-sided --verify replay over every case ical4j passes. The first replay flagged 19 of 1420 and all 19 were defects in my own classifier, not in ical4j (rule 49, ninth firing, this time on the check added to make the finding trustworthy): six were the no-dedup mutation re-scoping BYSETPOS, two were the WEEKLY model ignoring COUNT and UNTIL. After fixing both, 0 of 1420, and the failing-side counts did not move. Published as finding 075 with a supersession note added to the top of 051. Also corrected RESULTS.md: the published ical4j row summed to 1726 where every other row sums to 1727; the measured fail_prefix is 1, not the published 0. Suite green (33 files, 0 failed), cases_id unchanged. Nothing sent outward.
